text: Thank you for confirming your symptoms. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any fever, joint pain, or fatigue accompanying these blisters and ulcers? Also, when did you first notice these symptoms appearing?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You recently started captopril and stopped meloxicam; were these medication changes coincident with the onset of the blisters and oral ulcers? Please also describe the appearance of the forearm lesions—do they look like tense bullae or flaccid vesicles?
